description:
A multiplayer environment for coding with teammates and agents.

Delta brings teammates and coding agents into one shared thread. Your conversations and code live in the same place, and every change is anchored to the reasoning behind it, so the decisions and prompts that produced the code stay readable alongside the results.
Work in the Delta app or from your terminal; DeltaDB keeps both in the same thread. The version control system records every edit with the conversation behind it, and a thread shared from Claude Code can be joined from the Delta app, and the other way around.
Invite teammates into the same thread to review, comment, and work alongside the agent in real time. Comment on the conversation or any line of code, and the feedback stays anchored as the work evolves.
✨ New this release
- Search your organization’s threads by name, title, summary, and keywords from the cmd-t thread finder, the cmd-k palette, the organization threads overview, and delta thread search; the thread finder and palette list threads that aren’t on this computer yet in a separate section.
- Soft compaction is now available to everyone and is the default for new threads. It frees up context by trimming old tool results without making an LLM call.
- Right-click or hold the back arrow to navigate to a thread’s parent or siblings without opening the sidebar.
- Use Image Display in Thread settings to show message images as compact, uncropped thumbnails.
- Hovering a thread in the cmd-t thread finder or the cmd-k palette now shows its summary and when it was created and last active.
- Right-clicking a thread in the organization overview now lets you add it to your sidebar without leaving the overview, or copy its link.
- Notes can now be turned back into comments using Turn Into Comment.
- On desktop, right-click an HTML file link in a conversation and choose Open in Browser to open the local file.
⚡ Better than before
- Opening and catching up on large threads is now faster.
- Isolated subthreads’ worktrees now take far less disk space on macOS, and on Linux with Btrfs or XFS.
- You can now fork threads from the thread header, where the fork button opens a menu for creating a fork or reopening an existing fork, matching the review and merge menus, and use Fork Thread or Start Review from sidebar context menus.
- Agents can now respond to common interactive terminal prompts without restarting the command.
- View All Subthreads… now shows the whole thread family as a tree, preserving parent-child relationships when searching.
- Pull from Subthread… now opens a dedicated pull-only picker, where enter pulls changes from the selected subthread.
- The cmd-t / ctrl-t thread picker now shows thread status, type, project, and owner to help you tell results apart.
- Thread links pasted into messages and comments now appear as clickable links, showing the thread title when available.
- Thread-link tooltips now show titles and owner usernames and avatars when available.
- The terminal’s switch button is now available in every thread, and the @! terminal picker lists new terminals by project like the switch menu does.
- Claude Agent is better at showing charts and other images it creates inline in the thread, rather than linking to their files.
- Subthreads in the sidebar and subthread picker now show their creator’s avatar, dimmed while the creator is not focused on that subthread.
- The review diff’s project filter is now remembered for each thread after reopening it or restarting Delta.
- The Background Terminals menu now shows the starting worktree for commands run by Delta’s agent.
🔧 Fixes and reliability
- Files ignored by your global Git ignore file (core.excludesFile, such as ~/.config/git/ignore) are no longer captured in worktrees.
- Files Git tracks inside ignored folders now keep syncing after an editor saves them, and are picked up after git add -f.
- Editing a model provider credential saved in an older version no longer crashes Delta.
- Switching from a GPT model to a Claude model mid-thread no longer makes the next request fail with a “safety filter” error.
- Claude Agent now works in threads that have no project.
- Claude now receives messages from other threads while working instead of waiting until its turn ends.
- The welcome guide now runs on Claude Agent when you chose it during setup, instead of asking for a model provider.
- Files Claude Agent writes into new folders with its file tools now appear in the Changes panel.
- You can now copy links to positions and selections in subthreads when the parent thread is shared only with you.
- delta thread list, search, tree and watch now report a subthread as archived when you archived it or one of its parent threads, matching the sidebar.
- Choosing an option in an agent’s permission request with ctrl-shift-1 through ctrl-shift-9 now works with US keyboard layouts on Linux and in the web app.
- In the web app, typing ! at the start of an empty message opens a terminal when a Cloud Runner is selected and inserts the character otherwise.
- Stalled compaction requests to Zed-hosted OpenAI models now time out sooner.
- Creating a file or folder at a path listed in .delta/linked now explains that the path is linked, instead of creating a file that can’t be edited.
- The branch comparison picker no longer shows an error when a checkout has no default branch, and instead explains how to set one.
- A subthread that is waiting for another subthread to finish downloading now says so, instead of showing the other subthread’s progress.
- Deleting comments no longer leaves empty avatar rows or stray highlights behind.
- Deleting a highlight while its note is open no longer jumps to the bottom of the thread.
- Fork badges now appear only on the messages that create forks, not on surrounding messages included as context.
- Participant avatars now appear in all subthread tab toolbars, not just review tabs.
- Long project names in the sidebar are no longer cut off early when their header isn’t hovered.
- Long descriptions beside slash-command and model pickers no longer extend above the window.
- License text sections in the Open Source Licenses window now fold without corrupting the surrounding content.
